items.comment: A singable carol line: the scale runs in bars 5 to 7 sit comfortably under one hand and every strong beat agrees with the bass.

objections.problem: D repeated across the barline, then a C-D-E-D squiggle, makes bar 3 fussier than the plain bar 2.

items.comment: A clear five-finger tune with a left-hand answer in bar 4; the eighth-note turn in bar 3 is the one spot a beginner will stumble on.
Plain repeated quarters over a simple I-IV-V bass; ideal first-piece material.

objections.problem: F-G-F-G eighths wobble on the spot; the bar loses its pulse and the tune disappears.
Six eighths alternating E and F in one bar sound like a trill exercise, not a melody.
The same oscillation again, now D-E, in bar 7: a third bar in a row of identical wobbling.
E held on the downbeat over the G bass of a dominant bar sounds a little soft and unclear.
Stepping from G down to F on beat 4 weakens the arrival; holding the G would land the phrase.

items.comment: The harmony is sound, but almost every beat is split into a neighbour-note wobble at quarter = 120; I would rewrite bars 5 to 7 with plain repeated notes.
A shapely modal folk line rising to D and falling back, with open-fifth chords that support every strong beat.

objections.problem: The line circles C and D for two whole bars with no direction or goal.
D on strong beat 3 over a sustained C bass rubs mildly; C would sit better.
Eighth-note neighbour pairs fill bar 9 and keep the melody stuck between C and E.
Six running eighths end the passage; busy for a beginner and the phrase never settles.

items.comment: Harmonically safe, but the tune is lost under constant C-D-E wiggling; I would rewrite it with longer notes and a clear shape.
